name: deep-research
cost: Free and open source (MIT). Paid research providers or data plugins it coordinates cost extra
works_with: Claude Code, through the daymade-skills plugin marketplace
short: Runs research as a saved study, with parallel subagents, original sources behind every claim and a counter-review before the report.
what: deep-research writes research reports with strict format control and claim-level citations. A lead agent breaks the question into tasks, sends subagents to gather evidence, opens the original source for every load-bearing claim and runs a counter-review before the report is final. Each study is saved in the project with its sources, claims and rejected leads so later questions can reuse it. It can also coordinate reports from several AI research products and keep their original outputs.
who: People who write literature reviews or market and company research and want sources they can check. The process is heavy and keeps its own records, so it's overkill for a quick question.
needs: A way for your agent to search and open sources
A writable project folder, where the study records are kept
Accounts with other research providers, only if you want several routes

steps.title: Add the marketplace
steps.text: Inside Claude Code you can run `/plugin marketplace add daymade/claude-code-skills` instead.

steps.title: Install the skill
steps.text: The marketplace is called `daymade-skills`. Using the repo path as the name fails.

steps.title: Give it a brief
steps.text: Provide a report spec or template, then ask for a deep research report. Before it starts, it picks a topic mode (company or general research) and a depth (standard or lightweight).

try.label: From the README
try.text: Hand it your report template and ask for a market or company research report. It tells you the mode it chose and the as-of date it is working to before it searches.

watch: It can send work to other AI research products and data plugins. The skill says to check per-call charges first, put off any paid route you haven't approved, and tell you if a charge happens anyway.
It is told to use paid data sources you give it, such as a Crunchbase Pro account, for research on other companies.
It writes study records, archived sources and notes into your project folder. Its local scripts only record and check files and make no provider calls.
